notes: Equipment tree, SKUs and the per-unit question bank. Application code must never hardcode a SKU, a question or a BOM rule - everything the interrogation asks about a piece of equipment is defined here.

questions.prompt: What mount type is required?
questions.help: Drives the bracket and any adapter plate. If it varies across units of this SKU, split them into separate groups.

questions.prompt: What is the mounting surface?
questions.help: Determines anchors, backing and whether an adapter is needed.

questions.prompt: Is an adapter plate, back box or arm required on top of the base mount?
questions.help: Drop ceiling, metal deck and pole mounts almost always need one. Say 'unknown' rather than guessing - unknown flows into the assumptions block.

questions.prompt: Which adapter / arm part number?
Where is the mounting hardware coming from?

options.label: Customer already has it in stock

questions.prompt: What lead time has been quoted on the mounting hardware?
Mounting height above finished floor / grade (ft)?
What access equipment is needed to reach that height?
Who provides the lift?
Is this a new cable run or reuse of existing cable?
Cable type?
Estimated cable run length per unit (ft)?
questions.help: Measured path, not straight-line. Runs over 295 ft need a midspan or fiber - the tool will flag it.

questions.prompt: What pathway does the cable follow?
How much new conduit per unit (ft), and what type?
Conduit type?
Is any core drilling or penetration of a rated assembly required?
Where does this run terminate (IDF / MDF / closet name)?
Is the ceiling accessible along the full path?

options.label: No - hard lid or no ceiling access

questions.prompt: How is the device powered?
Have available switch ports and PoE budget been confirmed?

Is a 120V outlet present within reach of the device?
Indoor or outdoor?
Any environmental hardening required?
Door type and material?
What locking hardware is being used?
Who furnishes and installs the door hardware?
questions.help: This is the single most common scope gap on access control jobs. Be explicit.

questions.prompt: Is door or frame prep (cutting, drilling, raceway) required?
Request-to-exit method?
Door position switch required?
Does this door require a fire alarm interface or life-safety tie-in?
questions.help: Mag locks and some electrified hardware do. Tie-in work is usually the fire alarm contractor's, not ours - say so explicitly.

options.label: Yes - by the fire alarm contractor (others)

questions.prompt: Is there an ADA / automatic operator to integrate?
What programming or configuration is in our scope for this device?
Is end-user training included for this system?
Where is the equipment itself coming from?
questions.help: Sourcing status prints against every bill of materials line. 'To be ordered' with an unknown lead time is a schedule risk - say so.

flags.message: Copper run exceeds 295 ft. An extender, midspan or fiber path is required - the BOM will not be correct until this is resolved.
Cable pathway is unknown. Pricing assumes an accessible pathway; this is carried as an assumption.
Ceiling access is limited or unverified. Additional labour may be required for hard-lid or obstructed sections.
Access equipment requirement is unverified. Lift cost is not carried in this scope.
Mount height is above 14 ft but no lift is scoped. Confirm ladder access is genuinely adequate.
Magnetic locks require a life-safety release path. Fire alarm interface must be resolved before this scope is issued.
Door hardware responsibility is unassigned. This is the most common source of scope disputes - resolve before issuing.
Existing reader wiring is assumed serviceable but has not been tested. Replacement is not carried in this scope.
Switch port availability and PoE budget are unconfirmed. Additional switching is not carried in this scope.
